title: Mango and lime tart
subtitle: tropical mango and lime curd tart
excerpt: A mango and lime tart uses a curd made from fresh mango puree and lime juice, thick, orange, and intensely tropical. The lime keeps it from being cloying and adds a brightness that plain mango doesn't have on its own. It fills a pre-baked pastry case and sets firm in the fridge. This is a very good summer dinner party tart that requires no oven time once the pastry is baked.
sourceNotes: Mango curd, the mango equivalent of lemon curd, has been part of the British home baking repertoire since the 1990s, when mango became widely available year-round in supermarkets. The combination of mango and lime is deeply embedded in Caribbean, South Asian, and South-East Asian cooking, appearing in drinks, chutneys, and desserts across multiple traditions. Applied to the tart format here, it follows the same structure as the passion fruit curd tart, fruit juice cooked with eggs and butter to a thick custard, but uses blended mango pulp rather than strained juice.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before; the curd firms and flavour deepens overnight.
recipe.temperatureNote: for blind baking the pastry case only

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 190°C for blind baking; the mango curd is made on the hob

content.text: Mango and lime tart has a vivid orange curd filling that smells tropical and tastes actually sharp thanks to the lime. The curd is made on the hob from blended mango and lime juice, thickened with eggs and enriched with butter. Use Alphonso mangoes (from tins or fresh in season) for the deepest colour and flavour.

items.prepNote: flesh from ripe mangoes or Alphonso tinned mango

content.text: Blind bake the pastry and make the curd

Blind bake the pastry case at 190°C as standard (beans for 15 minutes, then 10 minutes without) and leave to cool. Blend the mango flesh until very smooth. Combine the mango puree, lime juice and zest, and sugar in a medium heavy-based saucepan. Whisk in the eggs. Cook over a medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 12 to 15 minutes until the curd has thickened significantly, it should coat the spoon thickly and leave a clean path when you run a finger across the back. Remove from the heat and beat in the butter piece by piece. Pour into the cooled pastry case and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until firm.
